extracted.intended_audience: institutions of higher education, scholars, and organizations seeking Mellon Foundation humanities grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for humanities grantmaking by the Mellon Foundation, describing priority topics, eligible activities, selection approach, and explicit funding restrictions. Intended to help applicants understand what kinds of projects and organizations the Foundation funds and how it approaches grant decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation-based, relationship-driven grant-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mellon Foundation staff review inquiry submissions and seek out organizations before inviting them to submit proposals, with most grants made through these invitations rather than through open competitive calls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied expectation that the Foundation initiates many funding relationships; unsolicited open-competition proposals are less common. Applicants should expect a relationship/developmental path rather than a purely competitive call-for-proposals process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher Learning — target audience and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions of higher education and scholars addressing crucial societal issues and promoting learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to work situated in higher education contexts and led by scholars/academic leaders focused on societally important questions and promoting learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher Learning — activities that broaden opportunities in the humanities
rubrics_metrics.description: Work broadening opportunities in the humanities through academic research, curricular development, extracurricular programming, internships, community partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundable activities include (but are not limited to) academic research, curricular development, extracurricular programming, internships, and community partnerships that materially broaden access to or opportunity in the humanities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanities in Place
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees that shine a spotlight on historically overlooked sites, communities and stories surrounding them, help broaden shared understanding, and open new paths to discover what unites us and what we can learn from one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on place-based projects that surface overlooked histories and community narratives, with an aim toward broadening public understanding and fostering connections across communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: American History and Culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars and academic leaders working to deepen understanding of American history and culture, advance new methods for scholarly interpretation, and elevate underrepresented perspectives in academia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for projects that both deepen scholarly interpretation (including new methods) and intentionally elevate underrepresented perspectives within American history and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding restrictions / ineligible activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation does NOT fund: Tuition; K-12 education and programming; Fundraising events; Direct unrestricted funding for individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should avoid requests for the listed ineligible items; grants are intended for charitable and/or educational purposes and not for tuition support, K–12 work, fundraising costs, or direct unrestricted individual support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants designated for charitable and/or educational purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are designated for charitable and/or educational purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested activities and budget items should demonstrably serve charitable or educational aims consistent with nonprofit grantmaking norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection approach — developmental, strategic, and equity-centered
rubrics_metrics.description: Mellon uses a more developmental, relational approach to grant-making rather than purely competitive review: identifies promising organizations and scholars; builds long-term relationships; strategic alignment with foundation's evolving priorities; equity-centered approach to scholarship and humanistic inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful proposals or partnerships are likely ones that align strategically with the Foundation's priorities, demonstrate potential for long-term relationship-building, and reflect equity-centered practices in scholarship and inquiry. Applicants should emphasize alignment, sustainability of relationship, and equity commitments.
